The federal carrier and overlapping split references remain table-only; no geometry repairs or count allocations. All307 raw reporting rows, earlier303-reference release and351 municipal decisions remain in complete downloads. Invalid Wayland municipal geometry remains held. No rates, county allocations, source repairs or unique-person claims.

MI.boundary_label: Official State of Michigan 2026 election-cycle precinct boundaries
MI.notes: Exact structured identities qualify all 35 Bay and 23 Isabella official precinct features for direct native counts. Rates remain withheld because native registration components are not defined. City of Clare's positive Isabella row cannot use the whole CountyFIPS 035 official polygon; four zero rows are official Gratiot/Midland precincts.

MN.boundary_label: Full unchanged native September18,2026 reference; not certified legal precincts
MN.notes: All4105 source statistics rows now explicitly report, including32 observed zeros. Source conflicts and electorate excesses remain literal; no precinct rate, geometry repair or certification inference.

NH.boundary_label: Official municipal ward display references in four New Hampshire cities, not certified 2026 legal precincts
NH.notes: Manchester12, Concord10, Nashua9 and Dover6: all37 held native ward reports now have direct references. Counts, source disagreements, separate federal-only fields and all prior31 shapes remain unchanged. Dover uses the independently state-published2022 NHGRANIT ward product, literal district labels, native3437 and declared inverseESRI108190; not old layer5, FID-as-ward or nativeFIPS-as-county. All1987 new vertices/cyclic edges and15 native pairs are checked, with no native Dover overlaps. Six Manchester and fourteen Concord overlaps remain unrepaired. Four cities only, not statewide/county totals or certified2026 legal precincts; no allocation or analysis rates.

DC.boundary_date: 2019-named reference selected by the official 2026 app
DC.next_action: Review outstanding ballots and updated certification; verify reference changes and all native contest-accounting differences; acquire group-specific denominators.
DC.notes: DC Council-chair plurality margins, not the RCV delegate contest or a federal House result. Complete precinct candidate rows reconcile with native per-precinct JSON and citywide JSON/XML. Separate ballots/registration reconcile independently; displayed fractions are provisional election-night shares, not final turnout or demographic rates. Local-contest accounting differences remain in the audit, never repaired or allocated. The official 2026 app explicitly selects its 2019-named embedded precinct reference; this is not newly surveyed/certified 2026 geography or a cross-election stability claim. Three source-boundary overlaps affect five precincts: ambiguous strips are withheld from both precincts, not assigned. Counts still describe whole precincts, never clipped-area allocations. Full original boundaries and the excluded-area mask are downloadable. All complete originals, including every CSV contest, XML/PDF and native reference bundle, are retained with receipts. Outstanding ballots and source/reference review remain.

ID.next_action: Obtain official county reporting-unit crosswalks, resolve reference overlap slivers and separately reported pooled-ballot scope. Resolve Twin Falls registration and other source ballot disagreements before enabling withheld rates. No ID-only matching or vote allocation.
ID.notes: All 986 House reporting-unit returns reconcile to complete county summaries and both district candidate APIs. 448 units map by unique complete county precinct-name sets and explicit congressional district to the official 2026 Idaho SOS reference. Only case, punctuation and numeric padding are normalized; no token reordering, aliases, ID decoding or vote allocation. Counties with inconsistent scope or any reference overlap above the audited tolerance are withheld. Separately reported absentee/early units remain unmapped; no pooled votes are allocated. Candidate votes are not turnout. Separate unofficial ballots/registration and all provisional fractions and withholding flags remain in the full download. These are source reporting units joined to reference precincts, not proof of complete residential all-ballot returns or demographic participation. Every original result workbook/PDF/API, every native and geographic GIS feature, unmatched return and county/geometry audit is retained.

ND.next_action: Resolve Morton parent IDs and Towner malformed precinct code with official crosswalk evidence; obtain precinct electorate denominators and certified returns.
ND.notes: Official 2026 House reporting-unit returns reconcile to all 53 counties and statewide totals. The official layer explicitly describes 2026 election precinct splits; its CountyID and Precinct fields must match each county's complete reporting set. All parts are dissolved into one geometry per reporting unit, with votes counted once. Morton is withheld for conflicting county IDs; Towner is withheld for a malformed extra precinct code. Native Esri ring roles preserve holes that the service's GeoJSON export misgroups. Area-preserving topology repairs are individually audited. Overlay processing uses a 1e-9-degree coordinate grid. Ambiguous overlapping boundary strips are excluded from both precincts, leaving state fallback colors there. Votes still describe entire reporting units, not clipped-area allocations. The full original boundaries and ambiguity mask are downloadable. No distinct mapped reporting-unit polygons overlap beyond the audited numeric tolerance. Unofficial candidate votes are not turnout. Separate ballot counts have no precinct denominator; all rates are withheld.
